source: Minchat Shai on Exod 5:15 (the double-stroke ruling)
claim_en: lama TAASE kho la-avadekha ('why do you DEAL thus with your servants'): the do-word carries the TWO-STROKE mark (the doubled stroke) — and MS rules its law: 'though it has a melody like the drop-mark, it does NOT pause — for it binds and ROLLS with the word after it' — and the stream carries the mark exactly where he rules it (checked), one of the DOUBLE-STROKE'S FIVE stations in the whole Torah (the stream's complete census): Isaac's 'bring it NEAR to me' at the stolen blessing (Gen 27:25), the beaten officers' cry HERE (5:15), the strange fire 'which He had NOT commanded' (Lev 10:1), the spies' 'were it not BETTER for us' (Num 14:3), and Nobah's villages (Num 32:42): the Torah's rarest stroke, five verses of trouble, and MS's ruling lands on the one in the officers' mouths.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:12/5:18 (the two Babel-pairs)
claim_en: The BABEL DOUBLE: ve-tokhen LEVENIM titenu ('and the count of BRICKS you shall give') — the bare bricks-word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah: BABEL'S 'come, let us brick bricks' (Gen 11:3) and Pharaoh's quota here (census checked; the Kitzur: 'whatever they built by day FELL by night — levenim nafelu,' the Isaiah third named, and the tower's three thirds); AND va-YAFETZ ha-am ('and the people SCATTERED,' 5:12) — the scatter-word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah: 'and the LORD SCATTERED them' from Babel (Gen 11:8) and the straw-scattering here (asserted; the Kitzur's Saul-third named — 'the scattering that undid a kingdom'): the letter binds Egypt's brickyard to Babel's twice over, in two different words, both exact pairs — the empire that makes bricks of men inherits the tower's vocabulary.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:8 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: hem TZOAQIM lemor ('they are CRYING, saying: let us go sacrifice'): the crying-participle stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — ABEL'S BLOOD ('your brother's bloods are CRYING to Me from the ground,' Gen 4:10) and the quota-cry Pharaoh mocks here (census checked) — and the Kitzur carries the dark completion: 'what you lack of the brick-count — set your own BODIES in the building: and this is crying-to-Me-from-the-ground' — the walled-in children heard in Abel's word-form: the letter files the empire's masonry under the first murder's grammar.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 5:22 (the manuscript Masorah's three spellings; the Ramah; the Meiri); Kitzur on 5:22
claim_en: lama HAREOTA la-am ha-ze ('why have You DEALT ILL with this people'): the manuscript Masorah MS quotes counts THREE why-dealt-ill stations, EACH SPELLED DIFFERENTLY — this one lean-yod lean-vav with a FULL final he (the Ramah's letter-arithmetic quoted in extenso; the Meiri and the Oil-of-Gladness book concurring; the Hilleli's 'Yerushalmi' short variant named), Moses' second at the camp ('why have You dealt ill with Your servant,' Num 11:11 — no final he), and ELIJAH'S at the widow's son (1 Kgs 17:20 — the full-vav form): the Torah-side pair verifies exact, both tokens unique (checked); and the Kitzur binds the file: 'both times Moses erred in this tongue... and the answer ata tireh — NOW you shall see — hinted he would not enter the land'; the Moses/Elijah parallels named (the angel at the son / the widow's son revived; the ascent on high / the storm to heaven): one question, three spellings, two prophets.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 5:7 (the Masorah-printer's error; Minchat Kohen's confusion)
claim_en: ki-TEMOL shilshom ('as YESTERDAY and the day before'): written FULL 'in the Hilleli copy and all precise books, like its neighbor close by' — and MS files the transmission-failure: 'the PRINTER of the Masorah erred, as I wrote at the Vayetze portion — and the Minchat Kohen went astray in ALL the places' (the chain naming its own broken links): the census verifies the full form's exact Torah-three — Laban's changed face ('not as yesterday,' Gen 31:2) and the two quota-verses of this chapter (5:7, 5:14 — checked): the yesterday-word of the changed regime, full at all three stations, with two printed authorities corrected en route.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:14 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: gam TEMOL gam ha-yom ('both YESTERDAY and today'): the both-yesterday phrase's one Torah station (adjacency checked) — its Scripture-twin at SAUL'S TABLE ('why has the son of Jesse not come, both yesterday and today?', 1 Sam 20:27) — and the Kitzur binds them: 'when they could not complete the brick-quota they HID, so as not to be beaten — the way DAVID hid': the beaten officers of the quota and the hunted harpist share one time-phrase: the letter files hiding-from-power under its own two-day clock.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:8 (the Masorah's pair; Ruth)
claim_en: TEMOL SHILSHOM ('yesterday and the day before'): the bare pair's one Torah adjacency here (checked) — its Scripture-twin in RUTH ('you came to a people you knew not yesterday or the day before,' Ruth 2:11) — and the Kitzur draws the two roads whole: 'Ruth came to an unknown people and they DREW HER NEAR — therefore the redeemer came from her; Israel came to an Egypt that knew them not, and they PRESSED them and enslaved them and threw their sons to the Nile — therefore MOSES came from them, who struck them with ten plagues, took their wealth, and drowned them': hospitality and oppression, each paid in its own coin, timed by the same two days.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:7 (the Masorah's three)
claim_en: ha-LEVENIM ('THE bricks'): the definite bricks-word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — 'to brick THE BRICKS' (5:7) and 'the count of THE BRICKS' (5:8), both in Pharaoh's decree (census checked) — the Kitzur's Masorah-three closing with Isaiah's brick-altars ('burning incense upon THE BRICKS,' Isa 65:3) and the tradition named: 'MICAH came out from under the bricks' — the child pulled from the quota-wall who grew into the idol-shrine (the fault-chain the priest-file of exo_02 already carries): the bricks of the decree, the bricks of the census, and the brick-altar of the apostasy — one definite article, three stations, the chain's arc from quota to shrine.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:9 (the Masorah's pair; the prayer-intent homily)
claim_en: ve-al YISHU be-divre shaqer ('let them not TURN to false words'): the turn-word's one Torah token (census checked) — its Scripture-twin 'they TURN, and there is none to save' — and the Kitzur turns the pair into the chain's prayer-law: 'those who do not intend in their heart what they utter with their mouth — of them it is said: they turn and none saves; but those whose heart stands behind their mouth — of them: you shall call, and the LORD will answer' (David's without-lips-of-deceit named): Pharaoh's sneer at the sacrifice-words becomes the tradition's measure of every prayer: the machine notes the misdirected cry of this chapter (the officers cry to PHARAOH, 5:15 — the cry of 2:23 went higher).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:23 (the Masorah's pair; David likened to Moses)
claim_en: ve-HATZEL lo hitzalta ('and DELIVER — You have not delivered'): the deliver-infinitive's one Torah token (census checked), doubled against its own negation — the chapter's last words are an indictment; the Kitzur's pair: DAVID'S 'you shall surely pursue... and SURELY DELIVER' (1 Sam 30:8 — the same infinitive-absolute, there a promise kept) — 'David is likened to Moses, as we explained at the believed-verse' (the two-shepherds file, exo_04): Moses' deliver-doubling in accusation, David's in assurance — the machine files the darkest close of the run: the deliverer telling the Sender the deliverance has not begun (6:1's answer armed, one verse over the border).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:9 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: TIKHBAD ha-avoda ('let the service be HEAVY'): the be-heavy word's one Torah token (census checked) — its Scripture-twin the psalmist's 'day and night Your hand was HEAVY upon me' (Ps 32:4) — the Kitzur: 'teaching that he made it heavy upon them BY DAY AND BY NIGHT'; and the machine files the kaved-word's triangle closing in on the book: the heavy MOUTH (4:10, Moses' plea), the heavy SERVICE (here, Pharaoh's decree), the heavy HEART (7:14, armed — the same root the hardening file will conjugate): the word that weighed the famine and the funeral-camp in Genesis now weighs the tools of the oppression.

The chapter's letter-file, MS's rulings on the stream's own letters: TEVEN ('straw,' 5:7) — 'on SIX DOTS' (the two three-dot vowels — checked: the straw-word pointed entirely in triads); ve-QOSHESHU ('and gather,' 5:7) — the shin on a simple sheva, the token Torah-unique (asserted); ve-CHATAT amekha ('and the sin of your people,' 5:16) — the Masorah: 'unique, and SOFT' — the officers' ambiguous last clause (whose sin? the readings' hearings named) carried with an undotted letter (asserted); shamu ALEHEM ('set over them,' 5:14) — lean yod with the Masorah, Minchat Kohen, and the Ramah, the sign filed at Vayigash (asserted); lama's soft mem and ha-ZE's dotted letter at the why-verse (5:22); el-PARO with the dotted pe (5:15): seven rulings riding the decree's own vocabulary.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 5:3/16/17; Minchat Shai (named-only remainder)
claim_en: The remainder, named-only with one count-check: NIRPIM atem NIRPIM ('IDLE — you are IDLE'): the idle-word doubled in Pharaoh's one verse (checked in-verse: exactly two) — the readings on the doubling named (idle from the service; idle from the words themselves — the king quoting the feast-request BACK, 'therefore you say: let us go sacrifice': the court-script's own words in the enemy's mouth, twice in the chapter, 5:8 and 5:17); NIQRA in gematria 'a YEAR' ('hinting the ten plagues would run inside one year' — the tradition's calendar, named); NATAN four ('Pharaoh who GAVE no straw SANK in the sea and went down among the slain — but he who GIVES of his bread, his waters are faithful' — the four-station give-word file, Scripture-wide, named); and VE-YAASU three ('in reward for THAT SERVICE they merited to MAKE the Tabernacle and MAKE the passover' — the make-word's wage, named): the chapter of unmade bricks closes its files on the makings to come.
